notes: Invoice INV-1005 and receipt REC-1005 both explicitly reference PO-1005, indicating a purchase order should exist for this transaction, but no PO document was provided in the case file, so it is flagged as missing rather than assumed exempt. Amounts (59,000 INR) are consistent across invoice, bank statement, ledger entry, and receipt, and the bank statement narration ties the NEFT settlement directly to INV-1005, supporting payment linkage. However, the receipt is dated 2026-07-18, three days before the invoice date of 2026-07-21, which is an unexplained date-sequence anomaly that internal amount/vendor consistency does not resolve. Tax amount (9,000 INR) is only explicitly itemized on the invoice; the bank statement, ledger entry, and receipt bundle it into the gross figure without separate breakout, which is noted but not treated as missing evidence since these document types are not expected to itemize tax. The successful bank settlement does not by itself confirm any payment-terms conditions beyond what the receipt independently documents. Overall the transaction is reasonably well-documented on the payment side but weakened by the absent PO and the receipt/invoice date inconsistency.
